# DeepSeek V4 Lightning Matrix Ceiling

Date: 2026-08-04

Status: schedule-ceiling `GO`; no production or FP4 promotion.

## Scope

This packet asks one deliberately optimistic question before implementing the
official packed indexer cache: can Apple simdgroup matrix instructions remove
enough of the current 64-head x 128-dimension arithmetic to leave a credible
budget for FP4 decode?

The candidate consumes an F16 query rounded once per layer and the existing F16
K cache. Eight simdgroups cover 64 heads x 8 rows. It is not official Q/K FP4
QAT, does not consume packed bytes, and has no production caller. The current
cooperative F32-query/F16-key scorer remains production and the differential.

## Identity

- Base before the candidate: `92bff19974a7257d6939141c0d34b0807dbcb57d`.
- Candidate source and this packet are captured by the same checkpoint commit.
- Hardware: MacBook Pro `Mac16,5`, Apple M4 Max, 16 CPU cores, 128 GB unified
  memory.
- OS: macOS 15.6.1 (24G90), Darwin 24.6.0 arm64.
- Rust: `rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14)` and
  `cargo 1.97.1 (c980f4866 2026-06-30)`.
- Metal: Apple metal 32023.864 (`metalfe-32023.864`), target
  `air64-apple-darwin24.6.0`.

No model weights are used. Keys, queries, and weights are deterministic
production-shape synthetic values.

## Frozen Protocol

CX design session `019fc50a-a944-7c60-9ac8-8083aad4b983` froze this protocol
before the candidate kernel was written:

- Warm alternating current/candidate calls, then retain raw
  current/candidate/current samples at 16,384, 65,536, and 262,144 rows.
- At 16,384 rows, candidate regression must be no greater than 0.05 ms/layer.
- At 65,536 rows, midpoint saving must be at least 0.15 ms/layer.
- At 262,144 rows, midpoint saving must be at least 0.80 ms/layer, candidate
  median must be at most 1.30 ms, and candidate p95 must be below both current
  medians.
- Query F32-to-F16 conversion is measured separately; it is not hidden in one
  scorer arm.
- Candidate output must repeat bit-for-bit and match an independent CPU oracle
  over F16-rounded operands. Tail groups, batched queries, tensor offsets,
  visibility, ReLU boundaries, selector ties, and nonfinite fallback are named
  correctness gates.

Exact performance command, run twice:

```bash
cargo test --release -p qwen-llm --lib \
  deepseek_v4_metal::tests::profile_lightning_matrix_ceiling_at_far_context \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

Correctness command:

```bash
cargo test --release -p qwen-llm --lib \
  matrix_ceiling_lightning_scores_ -- --nocapture
```

## Correctness Evidence

- F16-rounded CPU oracle: maximum absolute error `1e-9`, relative RMS
  `1.9e-8`.
- Current F32-query differential at every profile depth: maximum absolute delta
  `3.69e-7`, relative RMS approximately `3.005e-4`.
- Candidate repeats are bit-identical.
- Named tests cover 1/7/8/9-row tails, 128 batched dense F16 queries, nonzero
  tensor offsets, negative visibility, positive/negative/zero ReLU inputs,
  large-margin top-512, exact ties with lower-row stability, and nonfinite
  selector fallback.
- Pure existing validators cover SIMD width 32, 256-thread capacity, 4,096
  threadgroup bytes, and every u32 shader-offset product.

Formatting, patch whitespace, all-target checking, and strict release
qwen-llm all-target/all-feature Clippy pass.

## Decision

Every frozen schedule gate clears in both campaigns. The candidate establishes
approximately 1.585 ms/layer of terminal budget and justifies implementing an
official packed FP4 shadow. It does not prove that packed decode fits that
budget. The next experiment must include official Q/K quantization, packed K
decode, and per-layer Q work in timing and compare decisions against a
packed-semantic oracle before any production or snapshot-v2 migration.
